Density measured by drainage method is 6.78 g/cm³ (~14 % lower than pure iron 7.87 g/cm³). Austenite matrix composition measured by EDS (Table 2): S1000 ~20.97Mn-9.30Al-2.04Ni-3.24Cr-1.17C, S1050 ~21.09Mn-9.00Al-2.19Ni-3.16Cr-1.22C, MHT ~20.76Mn-9.46Al-2.01Ni-3.10Cr-1.15C (Fe balance); C content in austenite was calculated from lattice parameter equations because EDS is unreliable for C.
alloys.description: A single low-density austenitic steel produced by vacuum induction melting, alloyed with light Al in an Fe–Mn–C base together with Ni and Cr additions to obtain high strength, ductility and toughness; the entire study is conducted on this one nominal composition.

source.reason: The nominal composition Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr (analyzed Fe-20.3Mn-8.6Al-1.4C-2.1Ni-2.9Cr) is the only material studied; all heat-treatment conditions are applied to this same ingot, so a single alloy entity is defined.

paper.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
paper.paper_scope: Establishes the microstructure–mechanical-property relationship of a single Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr low-density steel by comparing single-stage heat treatments (S1000, S1050, and S1100 for tensile comparison) with a multi-stage heat treatment (MHT), focusing on how grain-boundary engineering (elimination of intergranular Cr7C3 precipitates plus a high fraction of special boundaries) improves impact toughness while maintaining high strength and ductility.
paper.title: Improving impact toughness of Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr low-density steel by optimizing grain boundaries via multi-stage heat treatment without compromising high strength and ductility

The Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr steel subjected to single-stage heat treatment at 1000 °C/3 min + quench is a distinct studied sample (grain size 3.17 μm, 71.7 % special boundaries, intergranular Cr7C3, impact energy 29.2 J).

The Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C–2Ni–3Cr steel subjected to the multi-stage heat treatment forms a distinct sample (grain size 7.31 μm, 71.2 % special boundaries, impact energy 55.1 J, YS 910 MPa, UTS 1076 MPa, TEL 50.9 %).

unmapped_findings: The ingot was homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h, then hot rolled at 1050–950 °C to a 6 mm sheet followed by air cooling to room temperature; this hot-rolling pre-treatment is common to all heat-treatment conditions and is not treated as a separate differentiating process.
The measured density of the steel (drainage method) is 6.78 g/cm³, about 14 % lower than that of pure iron (7.87 g/cm³).

Within the MHT route an intermediate heat treatment at 750 °C for 15 min leads to the distribution of many precipitates at the grain boundaries, which increase the stress in non-twinned regions and provide more twin nucleation sites (Fig. 9); this intermediate step is part of MHT rather than a separately reported sample.

The paper reports that the microstructure of all studied steels comprises an austenite matrix with nanoscale κ-carbides (3–10 nm), a small amount of B2 (20–160 nm) in S1050 and MHT, and intergranular Cr7C3 in S1000 only.
